text:
Elaine: Heads-up — I found a batch of ephemeral CSRs created against signing-service in eu-west around 03:12 UTC. Subjects look normal but the requestor field is 'proxy-provisioner' which seems unexpected.
Kishore: Can you paste the CSR subject + thumbprint? also which service account showed up in audit logs?
Elaine: subject=CN=svc.proxy.edge.eu-west, O=redwood, SAN=proxy.internal; sha256=9a3f...
Elaine: Quick audit snippet from signing-service: ```2026-03-18T03:12:05Z INFO RequestReceived uid=6f2a authn=proxy-provisioner region=eu-west action=create_csr```
opsec-bot: alert: csr-anomaly(eu-west) — 6 events in 2m for subject pattern 'svc.proxy.edge.*' (rule: ephemeral-csr-spike). See /alerts/6739451234
Samir: @kishore we did a tiny RBAC change last night to allow the proxy-provisioner role to call signing-service for canary nodes — could be related.
Kishore: Right — I added a scoped allow for signing:create_csr for the canary pool at 02:45. It should only allow CN pattern 'canary-*' though. I pushed the policy quickly; maybe the glob was too permissive.
Jason: If the policy glob was wrong it'd explain the requester showing as proxy-provisioner. Can we confirm whether the CA actually signed these CSRs or they were only accepted into the queue?
Elaine: Two of them show signed==true in the audit. Signed certs were issued with a 1h TTL.
Kishore: Oof. Immediate steps: 1) revoke issued certs 2) restrict the updated RBAC policy 3) gather KMS decrypt logs for the signing-key for that timeframe.
Samir: I'm running the revoke now: ```./signingctl revoke --region eu-west --selector "subject:svc.proxy.edge*" --reason "ephemeral-csr-misissue"```
Elaine: Revoke command completed — shows 2 certs revoked. I also exported their serials: SER=0x4a2f..., 0x4a30...
Jason: Forensics checklist: pull signing-service audit, KMS:Decrypt events (key_id=signing-key-eu-west), IAM:policy-change events, and edge-proxy logs that requested the certs.
Kishore: Query I'm running against GAIA audit store: ```SELECT * FROM audit_logs WHERE resource='signing-service' AND time >= '2026-03-18T02:40' AND time <= '2026-03-18T03:30' AND (action LIKE '%create_csr%' OR action LIKE '%kms:Decrypt%')```
opsec-bot: audit-query-result: 6 matching signing-service events, 3 kms:Decrypt events by principal 'svc-kms-eu-mid'.
Samir: That kms principal is our region-local signing agent — expected, but need to ensure the principal identity matches the service-account we intended.
Kishore: Also we should do configuration hardening: enforce CN pattern checks in signing-service (server-side validation), require client cert binding for critical sign calls, and log full request provenance (caller token id, originating SNI, source IP).
Elaine: Agreed. Propose short-term mitigations: remove the permissive RBAC rule (rollback to previous commit), rotate signing-key (or at least generate new intermediate and stop using current for issuance), and add a live reject rule for CSR subjects that don't match canary-*.
Jason: Rotating key will be disruptive — prefer issuing a new intermediate signed by the root KMS-protected key and switch issuance to new intermediate. That avoids re-encrypting root key material.
Kishore: I'll prepare the IAM rollback PR and a tighter policy: ```- Effect: Allow Action: signing:create_csr Resource: arn:.../signing-service/ca-1 Condition: StringLike subject: "canary-*"```
Samir: I'll own the immediate audit queries and packaging logs for incident. Elaine, can you capture the edge-proxy request traces (x-request-id) for those serials?
Elaine: On it — grabbing traces and will drop to the incident channel when collected.
Jason: Follow-ups: 1) Post-mortem item to add server-side CSR pattern checks 2) Telemetry: emit 'csr.requestor_identity' and KMS key usage id to Prom 3) Playbook update: if >3 unexpected CSRs in 5m, automatically pause signing for that region.
Kishore: Also add a policy test to CI that validates IAM condition patterns before apply. Saved us from this once.
opsec-bot: action_created: incident/6739451234 — Investigators assigned: @samir @kishore @elaine. Next update in 30m or on new findings. :lock:
